column5: deviation. The resolution's drain (`join_next` + `expect` until the set is empty) rests on the premise that every serving task has completed once every child has exited. I ran that literal shape: the inter-process proptest hung on it in roughly one plan in twelve (a 60 s bounded drain expired, so the test failed on `Elapsed`). Instrumented runs (I/O counts on the parent's link plus an EOF-logging wrapper on its control read) show the parked sessions completed their handshake exchange, opened and accepted no data stream, and never observed the control stream's EOF: they wait for a stream the dead child never opens, which the link contract leaves to the caller's timeout. So the wind-down grants this bounded grace, then aborts and joins. The grace is headroom over scheduling latency only; expiring costs sharpness (an aborted session counts as a possible loss), never a false failure.

negative control, committed. The witness pass's variant B (a panic on the serving path of accept-ordinal 3, the child's faulted retire in the retire-cut-at-first-byte plan) as a `should_panic` tripwire. Under the previous abort-and-discard wind-down this plan passes with the panic only in captured stderr; with panics swallowed in both settle loops it fails with `test did not panic as expected` (output in the commit message).
The probe knob lives on a sibling entry point rather than a `ProcPlan` field so the four reconstructed plans and the strategy stay untouched; `run_proc_plan` delegates with `None`.

The accept loop ends by a stop signal (the resolution's `close the listener rather than abort`): the task returns, dropping the listener, and hands its `JoinSet` back intact so no serving task's outcome is discarded.
Accept ordinal, so the tripwire can target one connection deterministically (children connect sequentially, so accept order is the child's phase order).

deviation, see the `SERVE_GRACE` row: bounded grace drain (with the resolution's `expect`), then `abort_all` on the contract-covered stragglers, then a join of every task that fails on any panic (the resolution's `JoinError::is_panic` alternative). An abort cannot mask a panic that already happened, and a serving task has no panic site after its session returns, so the join is total over panics.

Nit swept: `serve_errors` is now read after the serving tasks settle rather than at reap time, so an error landing between the last child's exit and the wind-down is counted; previously such an error was missed, which could only make `assert_party_invariants` stricter than the run warranted. Aborted stragglers count too, for the same conservatism.

Seed persisted by proptest during my iteration, when the literal drain expired on this plan (a plan with a straggling serving session). It is a legitimate plan, replays green under the landed wind-down, and exercises the straggler path, so it stays per the never-strip rule; the owner may prefer to drop it since the failure it recorded was an intermediate state of this branch, never a committed tree.

Population pin for the action alphabet, the shape of `membership_population_contains_churn`: 64 deterministic samples of `arb_local_actions`, counting a `Redact` only when an `Insert` precedes it, since `build_local` drops a `Redact` with nothing sent. Placed beside the strategy's primary consumer as the resolution offers. negative control: `Redact` weight 0 in `arb_actions` fails only this test (pairwise: 8 passed, 1 failed); output in the commit message.
Imports for the deterministic runner and the action alphabet the pin inspects.

Population pin for the schedule alphabet: 64 deterministic samples of `arb_schedule` at this suite's own `N_PEERS`/`MAX_EVENTS`, counting emitted `Redact` events (every emitted one is effectual by the shadow's construction, so no positional check is needed here). negative control: `RedactObservation` weight 0 in `arb_choice` fails only this test (multi_peer: 7 passed, 1 failed); output in the commit message.
Imports for the deterministic runner and the event alphabet the pin inspects.

Module doc restated as the ruling asks: the Open-time fork is the shadow's model, the live session forks after its preamble exchange (`prior_tree` is taken after `handshake::preamble` in `Rumors::gossip`), and the executor's guard is the consequence of the two forking at different points. I say `once its preamble exchange completes, some polls later` rather than `at its first poll` because with the tiny overlap buffer the fork lands several alternation rounds in; the entry's `first poll` was an approximation.

`Open` doc no longer states the fork as fact; it names the model and the live fork point, and points at the guard. Also notes a `Step` can complete a short session, which the executor already handles.

Guard comment carries its own justification (the model/protocol fork gap) instead of the borrowed `mirrors the serial executor's` one; the guard itself is unchanged per T13 (no assertion, no skip count, no ceiling).
`build_overlap_schedule` doc says what `valid by construction` means here: valid up to the model's imprecision, with the executor guarding the remainder.
The decorator's doc now cites its own witness and states that the conformance suite runs under this same decorator; the sibling-duplicate paragraph is gone with the duplicate (conformance-18).

`yield_once` doc restated without the `ReversingAcceptor` reference: the remaining reason for two copies is the feature seam (this crate-internal module must not depend on the public `conformance` feature), which still holds.

The resolution's (a): a `memory()` pair, one acceptor wrapped with batch 2, `join!` of a connector task and an acceptor task under `run_to_quiescence`; the connector yields four times between its two connects so the second arrival lands only after the acceptor has held the first and begun its patient wait. Asserts release order `21` and counter 1. negative control: a pass-through `accept` fails it (and both conformance reordering tests); `REORDER_PATIENCE = 0` (the Ready-only drain) fails only this test, so the witness pins the patient wait specifically. Outputs in the commit message.

Deletion annotated at the line that follows it: `ReversingAcceptor` (the Ready-only drain) and `reversing` are gone; `with_acceptor` stays for the lossy fixture. `grep -rn ReversingAcceptor src` is empty.
Nit swept: the batch depth both reordering tests pass is named once instead of a bare 3 at each call, matching the proxy suite's constant of the same name.

`reordered_accepts_conform` now decorates both memory ends with the shared `ReorderingAcceptor` (patient wait); its `reordered > 0` verdict holds (`PASS`), so per T21 the duplicate unifies rather than stays.

`reordering_acceptor_passes_independence` likewise; its `reordered > 0` verdict holds under the patient wait. The negative controls in this file do not use the reordering fixture and keep their verdicts (whole `conformance::` lib suite green).
The direction the entry names: conformance tests already depend on `crate::testing`; the shared decorator is imported from there. `pin` left the import list with the deleted acceptor.

deviation from the lane's hazard list (which opens only transport.rs and conformance/link/tests.rs under src/), isolated in its own commit so it can be dropped by itself. testing-infra-12's Resolution names this doc for rewriting, and once conformance-18 deletes `ReversingAcceptor` the sentence here is a ghost reference (a hard rule). Three doc lines, no code: the proof of the inversion firing is now the unit witness plus the conformance suite running under the same decorator. The `== 0` tripwire and the topology caveat stay as T21 rules.
`arb_fault` keeps its signature and delegates to `arb_fault_within(faults, max_cut)`, so the inter-process family can draw from its own bound without a second copy of the cut strategy.

Nit swept: the inter-process generator's bounds (seed messages, parent peers, children, sends, sessions) are named and used by `arb_proc_plan`/`arb_child_plan`, so the envelope derives from the strategy's own bounds the way `ENVELOPE_VALUES_PER_SIDE` does; the generated population is unchanged (same ranges).

The named inter-process bound, per connection (each child connection is its own link, so a cut's budget counts that connection alone). Measured: bootstrap 784, session 1055, final gossip 1459, retire 1749 bytes per endpoint; 2048 sits in the band [1749, 3498]. Under the previous draw from `0..MAX_CUT` (3072) about 43 percent of the family's cuts landed past the end of every connection; 3072 happens to sit inside the band too, so the old number was not vacuous, only unmeasured.

`arb_child_plan` draws every cut from `MAX_CHILD_CUT`. Committed seeds regenerate through this range (the file's own note on reconstructed counterexamples covers it); no new seed appeared; the reconstructed plans' literal offsets (max 2047) stay below the bound.
One metered connection: child side by closure, parent serving plain gossip as `run_proc_plan` does, both ends through `fault::metered`, widest endpoint reported.

The envelope: `child_main`'s clean path in-process over memory links. Judgment call on dominance: rather than one construction that maximizes every connection at once (impossible, since bootstrap wants the parent full before the child joins while a session wants the parent to have grown after), the parent gains a full complement of other-child sends before each connection, which dominates any real plan's per-connection divergence; the doc states that premise and the two-sided pin keeps it honest. Memory link rather than TCP so the number is deterministic.

Two-sided pin in the shape of `max_cut_spans_the_envelope_session`. negative control: `MAX_CHILD_CUT = 4096` fails the upper side (`is more than twice the child cycle's 1749 bytes`); `= 1` fails the lower side; outputs in the commit message.
`ByteMeter::read` exposes the read counter (the one a `read_cut` spends) so the asymmetric witness places its one-byte-short cut on the same accounting the cut uses, as the meter's doc promises.

The named bound replacing the literal 400. Measured clean fixture: A wrote 188, B wrote 191, B read 188; 256 sits in the band [191, 382]. The literal 400 fails the pin's upper side (more than twice the session), i.e. more than half the old family's cuts landed past the session's end.

The proptest body split into `run_severed` (the fixture and drivers, faults per end) and `check_severed` (the contract's assertions, unchanged in substance) so the deterministic witness runs the same drivers and the same checks as the generated family.

Clean metered run of the same fixture and drivers; the in-memory link and single-threaded driver make it byte-identical across runs (the lifecycle suite's marker witness rests on the same premise), which the witness relies on.
Two-sided pin. negative control: the former literal 400 fails it (`MAX_SEVER_CUT (400) is more than twice the fixture session's 191 bytes`); output in the commit message.

The acceptance's deterministic asymmetric case: B's read budget one byte short of a clean session, A `Ok`, B no `Ok` and terminal `Error::Epilogue`, then the full `check_severed` (certification holds). I first asserted only `B ends in Err`; a control with the budget exactly at the clean count still passed because B's remote-led driver errors on its next control read after a complete session, so the assertion now pins the class and the absence of any `Ok` at B. negative control: that exact-budget cut fails the tightened witness; output in the commit message.

Read cuts join the family on either side (optional, so the always-present write cuts keep their coverage), and the doc claims only what the family produces, pointing at the deterministic witness for the asymmetric case.
